evidence.deny_toml_says_closed: deny.toml lines preceding the ignore list explicitly state 'RUSTSEC-2026-0119 + RUSTSEC-2026-0120 (hickory-dns CPU-exhaustion + NSEC3 unbounded-loop) CLOSED 2026-05-19 at G-CORE-2-FP-1 via iroh 0.98 → 1.0.0-rc.0 bump; transitive hickory-resolver 0.26.0-beta.4 → 0.26.1 picks up the upstream fix. evidence.asymmetric_count: deny.toml ignore list: 17 unique RUSTSEC-IDs; supply-chain.yml --ignore list: 19 unique IDs; delta = {RUSTSEC-2026-0119, RUSTSEC-2026-0120}
evidence.rule_origin: This is EXACTLY the dual-config drift pattern §3.5g item 4 was codified to catch (added at R6 R2 methodology-critic 2026-05-13 after the original cargo-audit ↔ deny.toml mirror split surfaced)

findings.rule: §3.5g item 4 cross-tool config mirror — same-language dual-config rule-mirrors (deny.toml advisory ignore-list ↔ CI cargo-audit --ignore flags) MUST atomically update against same source-of-truth
findings.fix: Remove the two `--ignore RUSTSEC-2026-0119` + `--ignore RUSTSEC-2026-0120` lines from .github/workflows/supply-chain.yml:99-100. cargo-audit will then either pass (if the iroh-bump fully cleared the transitive) or fail with an actionable finding (which is what we want — silent ignores against a closed advisory hide regressions). The deny.toml comment 'cargo-deny warns on advisory-not-detected for stale ignores' confirms the workflow gate should self-correct.

findings.title: tests/phase_3_workspace/missing_docs_workspace.rs `full_missing_docs_sweep_no_warnings_workspace_wide` spawns `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` from within a `cargo nextest` test runner — recursive cargo invocation has known reliability footguns

evidence.concern: When invoked from `cargo nextest run --workspace`, the spawned `cargo doc` inherits a `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` + lockfile + may contend with the outer cargo's build graph. Empirically this pattern works when the outer cargo has already settled (the test is the LAST thing in the nextest run), but it's an implicit dependency on test-ordering that ci.yml does not enforce. Per the orchestrator-direct workspace pre-push verification memory (feedback_orchestrator_workspace_pre_push.md), this is exactly the kind of recursive-build hazard worth flagging.

findings.rule: L12 missing-docs verification mechanism robustness — the gate must be reliable not just present
findings.fix: No change required. CI is the authoritative invocation (ci.yml:222-226 runs `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` with `RUSTDOCFLAGS: -D warnings` as a top-level step, NOT via the recursive nextest path). The phase_3_workspace test is a belt-and-suspenders local gate that happens to invoke the same command; if recursive cargo is unreliable the top-level CI step still catches drift. The redundancy is intentional per pim-2 §3.6b end-to-end pin discipline.

findings.title: MSRV (1.95) clippy gate is intentionally NOT enforced — only stable runs clippy per ci.yml:140

evidence.ci_design: .github/workflows/ci.yml:134-141 — `# fmt + clippy only on stable to avoid MSRV-chasing lint churn; the # MSRV legs still build+test to catch accidental post-1.95 features.`
evidence.msrv_workflow_scope: .github/workflows/msrv.yml only runs `cargo build --workspace --locked` at 1.95 + the canonical fixture CID check; no clippy invocation
evidence.documented_rationale: Comment block at ci.yml:134-135 makes the design choice explicit + names the failure mode (lint churn) the choice avoids

findings.rule: L12 lens question asks about MSRV clippy; answer is 'NOT enforced by design'
findings.fix: No change. Adding MSRV clippy would require pinning a stable clippy lint set against the 1.95 toolchain, which both cargo and clippy actively churn — net effect would be CI breakage on every clippy bump unrelated to project code. The MSRV `cargo build --workspace` step in msrv.yml + the test suite running at MSRV in ci.yml's matrix legs (rust: 1.95.0) collectively catch the actual MSRV regression class (accidental new-language-feature usage). Linting at MSRV would add no signal that stable clippy doesn't already cover.
